findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the ADR deliverable (create/update the decision record for the rename) in the Design doc list so AC5's 'historical ADR record' exclusion has a concrete target.
evidence: AC5: 'returns no hit outside the historical ADR record'
Design: 'Docs/guides/runbooks/comments updated to the new word' — no ADR named
Context: 'OPERATOR DECISION (option c, 2026-08-12): RENAME our trigger'
findings.finding: AC5's verify grep excludes hits 'outside the historical ADR record', and Context cites an 'OPERATOR DECISION (option c, 2026-08-12)', implying an ADR documenting this decision exists or is to be created — but the Design section's documentation deliverable list ('Docs/guides/runbooks/comments updated to the new word') never names creating/updating an ADR. The grep-exclusion target in AC5 is therefore an uncovered/unspecified artifact.
scenarios: Executor runs the AC5 grep, finds a hit in an ADR that was never created/updated, and cannot tell if it is the sanctioned exclusion or a stale reference.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Design doc bullets: 'Record the rename decision in ADR <id> (the historical record AC5 excludes).' and reference that ADR path explicitly in AC5's grep exclusion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the retired-word occurrences in src/rebar/review_bot/app.py, reconcile.py, and the retrigger.py module docstring, and state explicitly whether each is updated to the new word or is a permitted descriptive residue; align AC5b's allowance with the actual surviving docstring lines.
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:176 '# A contributor `recheck-review` comment (ticket bb9b)'
src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py:25 '(a ``recheck-review`` comment, a re-push) could re-admit the change'
retrigger.py module docstring lines 1, 7, 52 reference `recheck-review` descriptively — AC5b names only 'the regex and the module docstring line that explains it' (singular, about the detector)
AC5 grep target omits src/rebar/review_bot/*.py; AC5b's verify grep only catches instruction-shaped lines
findings.finding: The plan's edit-set does not enumerate the retired-word occurrences in src/rebar/ code comments outside _guides/ (app.py:176, reconcile.py:25, and retrigger.py module docstring lines 1/7/52), and the AC grep scopes leave them unaddressed: AC5's grep covers only 'docs/ src/rebar/_guides/ AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md infra/' (excluding src/rebar/review_bot/*.py), while AC5b only flags src/rebar/ lines that 'instruct a contributor'. These descriptive comments would silently retain 'recheck-review'.
findings.location: Design > Changes ('Docs/guides/runbooks/comments updated to the new word'); AC5/AC5b
scenarios: A reviewer greps for the retired word post-cutover and finds it still present in bot code comments, unclear whether that is intended or a miss
findings.suggested_fix: Add these three files to the Changes list, update the descriptive comments to `rerun-llm-review`, and reword AC5b to name every surviving retired-word line (detector regex + the specific docstring line) rather than 'the module docstring line'.

The existing tests hardcode 'recheck-review' and the OLD near-miss forms ('recheck-reviews', 'pre-recheck-review', 'recheck-review-x'), which AC1 replaces with 'rerun-llm-reviews'/'pre-rerun-llm-review'/'rerun-llm-review-x'; the accepted/refusal message assertions also embed the retired word.
scenarios: Implementer edits retrigger.py, runs AC1's pytest, and the existing tests fail because they assert the old token/near-miss forms — the required test rewrites were never scoped

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the retired-token refusal obtains change_id/revision to post to, and whether the project guard / change-existence check must run before the retired-token refusal branch (reconcile the stated order with the fact that post_comment needs a re-anchored revision).
evidence: Plan: 'loop guard -> new-token match -> retired-token match (refusal branch) -> project guard -> eligibility -> reset'
Plan: 'it posts exactly one best-effort post_comment refusal and returns None'

In current retrigger.py the project guard (lines 306-309) precedes any Gerrit write, and post_comment needs change_id/revision which are only derived after get_change_event re-anchoring (lines 340-341); a refusal placed before those steps has no change_id/revision to post to and would fire on out-of-project changes
findings.finding: The plan's specified handler order runs the retired-token refusal branch before the project guard and before the change re-anchoring (get_change_event) that derives change_id/revision, but posting the refusal comment requires that re-anchored change_id/revision and should respect the project guard.
scenarios: A retired-word comment on a change whose project != cfg.project
A retired-word comment where change_key is missing/None
The retired branch attempting post_comment before get_change_event has resolved a current revision
findings.suggested_fix: Place the retired-token refusal branch AFTER the project guard and after get_change_event re-anchoring so it has a resolved change_id/revision and never replies on out-of-project changes; keep the new-token silent-skip early, and note that a retired-word comment on a non-matching project is a silent no-op like any other.

findings.finding: AC5's verify command `grep -rn "recheck-review" ...` scans `docs/` (which houses the historical ADR) yet the success condition says it 'returns no hit outside the historical ADR record' — the command as written will return the ADR hit, so a literal 'no hit' pass is impossible and the pass/fail boundary is a manual judgment rather than a deterministic command.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the ADR filename and change the command to exclude it: `grep -rn "recheck-review" docs/ src/rebar/_guides/ AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md infra/ | grep -v docs/adr/<file>.md` returns no lines.

findings.finding: The rename's Design 'Changes' edit-set omits the test files that hardcode the retired trigger string and its near-miss forms, which the rename must update.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Changes' bullet: 'tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger.py, test_review_bot_retrigger_attestation_6a81.py, test_review_bot.py — update trigger literals and the near-miss parametrize list to the new token (rerun-llm-reviews / pre-rerun-llm-review / rerun-llm-review-x).'

findings.finding: AC5b's verify `grep -rn "recheck-review" src/rebar/ | grep -v "_RETIRED_TOKEN_RE"` filters only lines containing the symbol name, but the Design and AC5b both permit the retired word to also survive in 'the module docstring line that explains it' — that docstring line will not contain `_RETIRED_TOKEN_RE` and so appears as an unfiltered hit, making the command's residue disagree with the two locations the AC declares legitimate.

The trigger-word rename is realized as a string-literal change (`TRIGGER_TOKEN`/`_TOKEN_RE` value `"recheck-review"`), and `TRIGGER_TOKEN` has no external structural referencers — the accept-path is exercised through the STRING literal in test fixtures. The plan's change inventory omits `tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger_attestation_6a81.py`, whose `_comment_event` default (`comment="recheck-review"`, line 52) drives the RETRIGGER_ATTESTATION_UNBLOCKED accepted path; after the rename that literal no longer matches `_TOKEN_RE`, so the attestation acceptance tests hit the retired-word refusal branch and fail.
findings.location: Design > Changes ('retrigger.py: ...'; 'Docs/guides/runbooks/comments updated to the new word.')
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Changes list: update every `recheck-review` STRING literal in test fixtures — `test_review_bot_retrigger_attestation_6a81.py` `_comment_event` default and summary text, plus `test_review_bot_retrigger.py` positive-form and near-miss parametrize lists — to `rerun-llm-review`, keeping at least one retired-word case that asserts the new refusal branch.
